item3_shared_basis_gap.reason: The control (2023 table) is internally consistent with the 2023 report: both its diagonals are as printed in the 2023 report, outstanding ties (38,860), and it has no outside column. Its -2,150 (-7.2%) gap has no named basis explanation in the pages (FX: all cells at closing rate, accounts claims incurred excludes the -570 FX effect; no '& prior' column; first-year cells are small, 8% of GWP, so it is not an ultimate/underwriting-basis table). The only candidate named difference, ultimate (UPR-inclusive) against earned, is not shared: in the 2024 table the end-2023 diagonal is 34,051 above what the 2023 report printed for the same cells (UY2023 +27,244, about 51% of the 53,283 gross unearned premium at end 2023, which looks like a loss ratio on unexpired risk; UY2022 +7,229, which cannot be unexpired risk as 2022 policies have expired), while the end-2024 diagonal ties to earned outstanding (75,447) and the UY2024 first-year cell 9,151 is only 5.6% of GWP, so the two diagonals in the year t table are on different bases and the control's are not. Even if the whole +34,051 were basis, the year t miss would still be -16.6m (-27%) after adding it back (11,227+34,051 = 45,278 vs 61,923). The control's gap is -2,150 (4.0% of the 53,283 gross UPR) against year t's -50,696 (60% of the 84,275 gross UPR at end 2024).
item3_shared_basis_gap.status: no (not the same gap; the control gap has no named basis explanation and the year t gap is mostly a restated prior diagonal)

4747_2024.rule_consequence: Control gap 7.2% is above 5% and no shared basis gap holds, so under the stated rule the 10% route is unavailable and the control does not tie on the 5% test; separate fact: year t miss is at least three times the control's. Under a 5% control threshold the control fails.
4747_2024.contradicts_premises: The year t miss is not a basis gap shared with the control: the 2024 table's own end-2023 diagonal differs from the 2023 report's by +34,051 (history restated, unexplained) and its cumulative paid row falls below the 2023 report's (2020 UY 4,843 -> 213). Both reports' outstanding tie to their balance sheets (38,860; 75,447).

Both tables exceed the accounts, which is the sign a release on the & prior years would give (the cells exclude it, the accounts include it): control +9,515 (110,268 vs 100,753), year t +7.7 (146.3 vs 138.6), so an & prior release of about 9.5 and 7.7 would close both, and the notes show gross prior-year releases in both years (2015 (32.2), 2016 (15.6)).
